Blog Review: Aug. 12

Shares

Early multiphysics; high-speed M-PHY; STCO for 3D-ICs; what EDA needs for AI; workload optimization.

August 12th, 2026 -

By: Jesse Allen

Synopsys’ Greg Sorber finds that multi-die designs that integrate chiplets on ever-larger substrates are pushing multiphysics upstream, blurring domain boundaries, and accelerating the adoption of AI tools and digital twins.
Cadence’s Sugandha Bansal introduces MIPI M-PHY’s ADAPT training mechanism that enables analysis of channel characteristics and refinement of equalization settings before high-speed data transmission begins.
In a podcast, Siemens’ Tova Levy chats with Intel Fellow Sujit Sharan about why system technology co-optimization is crucial for 3D-ICs and how standardized data exchange and cloud-based collaboration remain critical gaps.
Keysight’s Pedro Pires suggests organizations implement standardized data interfaces, ensure transparency in model training, and invest in orchestration platforms to get the most out of AI in EDA.
Arm’s Henry Wang shows how to teach AI coding agents to efficiently drive Arm workload profiling and optimization, with no human guidance beyond the initial prompt, and shares an example using feature-mean normalization.
Plus, don’t miss the blogs featured in the latest Automotive, Security & Edge AI and Test, Measurement & Analytics newsletters:
Accellera’s Alessandra Nardi explains why the semiconductor industry needs a common language for functional safety.
Technology strategy advisor Geoff Tate looks at how data center AI can keep growing, despite supply chain bottlenecks.
PDF Solutions’ Jonathan Holt shows why even the most sophisticated AI algorithm cannot compensate for fragmented data, absent governance, or siloed infrastructure.
Onto Innovation’s Huayuan Li, Alex Hong, Johnny Mu, Timothy Kryman, and Priya Mukundhan examine how critical process parameters and variations can impact reliability.
Teradyne’s Jeorge Hurtarte illustrates why heterogeneous integration redistributes where quality must be assured.
Advantest’s Don Ong sits down with ISIG CEO Salah Nasri to discuss how semiconductors are evolving from a product industry into an ecosystem industry.
Siemens EDA’s Reetika combines structural analysis with timing awareness and context-based classification to distinguish real RDC design risks from safe implementation choices.
Rambus’ Vincent van der Leest shows how multiple PCIe controllers and links can use a common security infrastructure while maintaining independent protection mechanisms.
Imagination Technologies’ Thomas Ferrere shows how to accelerate matrix multiplications while maintaining accuracy and reducing circuit area.
Synopsys’ Geert-Jan Schrijen, Peter Simons, and Dana Neustadter explore SRAM-based identity generation combined with functional safety and security mechanisms.
Keysight’s Doug Carson digs into the growing importance of peripheral interfaces in hardware threat models.
Infineon’s Kimia Azad shows why selecting the right power device class is a strategic decision based on mission life and cost.
Cadence’s Steve Brown observes that AI agents can understand design intent and implement meaningful portions of the design process.
Siemens’ Marc Hutner and Ron Press find that while human engineers created the breakthrough SSN architecture, AI helps maximize its value.
